name: Chambéry Tarot
description: Early 20th century French Tarot from Chambéry, Savoy. Three to five players; with four or five, partnerships form by Solo bid or dealer calling a King. Objective: win the majority of 68 card points (52 from counting cards plus 15 tricks and the discard). Uses 78-card French Tarot; trumps rank 21 down to 1; Fool may be shown once and added to team's tricks.

content.text: Early 20th century French Tarot from Chambéry, Savoy. Three to five players; with four or five, partnerships form by Solo bid or dealer calling a King. Objective: win the majority of 68 card points (52 from counting cards plus 15 tricks and the discard). Uses 78-card French Tarot; trumps rank 21 down to 1; Fool may be shown once and added to team's tricks.

Rules by the Club des Taroteurs in the Grand Café Emile Coudurier in Chambéry, capital of French Savoy, accompanying the 1902 Tarot français des fleurs (French Flower Tarot) by Fossorier, Amar & Cie. Savoy belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia until 1860; rules resemble Piedmont and Nice Tarot more than modern French Tarot.
Three to five; five preferred. With four or five, partnerships (Solo or called partner). With three, each plays for themselves.

A French-suited Tarot pack of 78 cards: 22 trumps (tarots) ranking 21 down to 1, the Fool (Fou), and 56 suit cards in four suits (King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, then Ace and numerals 10–2). The standard game uses the full pack; a shortened 62-card version (tarot simplifié) exists for three or four players.
78-card French Tarot pack; chips (50 points per player) optional for scoring.

Deal and play anticlockwise. Dealer rotates right after each hand. Five players: dealer gives packets of 5 three times around so each non-dealer gets 15 cards; dealer takes last 3 (18 total) then discards 3 face down. Dealer may not discard Kings, 21, or Fou; other tarots only if dealer would have no tarots left. Four players: each gets 19 cards (e.g. 5,5,5,4); dealer gets 6 last and discards 2. Three players: each gets 25 in five packets of 5; dealer gets 3 extra (28) and discards 3.

items.text: Four-Player Chambéry: Each player receives 19 cards (e.g. 5,5,5,4); dealer gets 6 last and discards 2. 72 card points total; tie at 36. Play with Solo/call or fixed partnerships (partners opposite).

Three-Player Chambéry: Each receives 25 cards in five packets of 5; dealer gets 3 extra (28) and discards 3. No partnerships, no Solo. 78 card points; players under 26 pay the difference (doubled if under 13).
Tarot simplifié (shortened pack): Remove 2, 3, 4, 5 from each suit (62 cards). Three or four players; different deal and scoring; see source for details.
